The ability to add digital versions of driver's licenses to iPhone looks set to expand to a 15th US state in the near future.

Apple currently lists 14 states, plus the territory of Puerto Rico, as supporting the feature, and backend resources now show another state about to join...

Many of us have long hoped for the day when we could ditch physical forms of identification like driver's licenses and passports and simply present digital ID through our iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be far off, but Apple took a first step back in 2021, when it announced plans to let iPhone users add a driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. Fourteen states have now adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend resources spotted by MacRumors indicate that Oklahoma is about to be added to that list.

We previously detailed the steps required to add a driver's license or state ID to the iPhone Wallet app. As we noted at the time, please note that digital IDs cannot completely replace physical documents, so we unfortunately still recommend continuing to carry the physical version with you.

That said, the digital version is useful in protecting your privacy at eligible TSA checkpoints, as well as when asked by businesses to show proof of age. The ID can confirm that you meet the age requirement without disclosing any personal information, such as your date of birth.
